# Environment

Every variable hubd reads, from the code the package ships. Set them in the environment of the process: the MCP client's server entry (`--env NAME=value`), the shell, the unit that runs mesh-sync.

## Where the hub is

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HUBD_DIR` | `~/.hubd` | The hub folder: cards, journal, tasks. Set, it wins over every other way of finding one. Unset, a hub at the older `~/.project-hub` is still found when `~/.hubd` does not exist. `hub doctor` says which rule chose the folder. |
| `PROJECT_HUB_DIR` | — | The old name of `HUBD_DIR`, read when `HUBD_DIR` is not set. |
| `HUBD_TEAM_DIR` | — | The team folder: queues, `AGENTS.md`, `subscriber-roles.json`. Set without `HUBD_DIR`, it is the hub folder too: a harness that names one directory means one directory. Unset, the team folder is the nearest folder above the working directory, up to 8 levels, that holds hub data, else the hub folder. |
| `HUBD_QUEUE_DIR` | — | The old name of `HUBD_TEAM_DIR`, read when it is not set. |

## Who is writing

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HUBD_NODE` | the host name, its first label | This node's name: in the names of the files it writes (`journal.<node>.jsonl`, `tasks.<node>.events.jsonl`, `queues/<role>.<node>.queue.md`) and in the ids of its messages. mesh-sync commits under it too, so set it where the sync runs as well. Lower case, letters, digits, `-` and `_`, at most 40. |
| `HUBD_TASK_ID_PREFIX` | the node's name | The prefix of new task ids (`<prefix>-<n>`), when the node's name should not appear in them. Existing ids keep theirs, and the numbers go on. |
| `HUBD_AGENT` | — | The author when a call names none. Over MCP it fills `agent`, `by` and `from`, with a four-character suffix per session, so two sessions on one machine never write as one; on the CLI it stands in for `--by` or `--agent`. A model's or a client's name is no author: the server ignores such a value, with a warning. Not used over HTTP. |
| `HUBD_SESSION` | the client's process and its start time | This session's id: the suffix above, and a reader name for queue cursors. Set it when a wrapper knows the session better than the process tree does. |
| `HUBD_SUBSCRIBER` | — | The reader name for queue cursors, so a reader that restarts goes on where it stopped; else `HUBD_SESSION`, else `HUBD_AGENT`, else the client's process. `hub watch` takes it as its cursor when `--as` is left out. |

## Limits

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HUBD_MSG_MAX` | `16384` | Bytes a queue message, a report or a task may hold; `0` lifts the cap. Cargo is refused at any size: a base64 or hex run over 2 KB, a git diff, a git bundle, a PEM block. |
| `HUBD_QUEUE_MAX_MSGS` | `50` | Unread messages a role's queue holds before a send to it is refused; `0` turns the limit off. Unset, `queue.msgs` in `limits.json` decides. An owner role, a role listed in `queue.exempt` and a role of rank `fleet` are never refused. |
| `HUBD_QUEUE_MAX_BYTES` | `262144` | Unread bytes, the same way; `queue.bytes` in `limits.json`. |
| `HUBD_MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS` | `40000` | Characters an MCP tool's answer holds before its long lists are trimmed, the journal first, and what was left out is named in `truncated`; at least 2000. `full: true` asks for everything. The CLI is never trimmed. |
| `HUBD_PRESENCE_SNAPSHOT_MS` | `300000` | How often at most, in milliseconds, a node republishes `presence.<node>.json` for the other nodes; at least 1000. Keep it under the shortest heartbeat TTL (15 minutes by default). |

## HTTP server

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HUBD_HTTP_PORT` | `8787` | The port of `hubd --http`; a port after `--http` wins. Set on its own, it turns HTTP on. |
| `HUBD_HTTP_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | The address `hubd --http` and `hub serve` bind. Keep it local behind a TLS proxy. |
| `HUBD_TOKEN` | — | The bearer secret, 16 characters or more; required unless multi-tenant. |
| `HUBD_MULTITENANT` | off | `1`: every token is a workspace of its own, at `tenants/<hash>/`; `hub serve` then takes `?t=<token>`. |
| `HUBD_RATE_LIMIT` | `120` | POSTs a minute from one client address; over it, 429. |
| `HUBD_MAX_TENANTS` | `1000` | Workspaces multi-tenant mode creates at most; over it, 403. |

## mesh-sync

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HUBD_SYNC_TIMEOUT` | `300` | Seconds a fetch or a push may take. `scripts/mesh-sync.sh` also reads `HUBD_DIR` and `HUBD_NODE`. |
| `HUBD_SYNC_PUSH_TRIES` | `3` | Pushes a run makes in all when another node's push wins the race; each one fetches and merges first. |

## Sensors and secrets

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HUBD_SENSE_DIR` | `<hub>/.sense` | Where `hub sense` keeps each head's sensor state. Node-local. |
| `HUBD_SENSE_ESCALATIONS` | `<sense dir>/escalations.log` | The file `hub sense` appends escalations to, one line each: the epoch, the head and the text, tab-separated. Point it at your monitor's file. |
| `HUBD_SECRETS_DIR` | `~/.hubd-secrets` | Where `hub secret` keeps values. Refused inside the team folder, which replicates to every node. |

## Set by hubd

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HUBD_WATCH_KEY` | — | In the environment of `hub watch --exec <cmd>`: the entry's hash, the same on every attempt, so a receiver can drop a repeat. |
